chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Zayd al-Shahham who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I go out from the Masjid and in my garment is a pebble.' He said: 'So return it, or throw it back into the Masjid.'

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: The Mosque (specifically the Sacred Mosque in this context)

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they leave the Masjid with a pebble stuck to their clothes?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific juristic ruling on removing minor natural elements like pebbles from the precincts of the Kaaba, emphasizing the sanctity of the site's soil. The Imam’s instruction to either return the pebble or discard it within the Masjid underscores the principle of preserving the integrity of the Sacred House’s environment, a view supported by Shia scholars who distinguish between permanent removal and temporary adherence. This ruling reflects the broader theological emphasis on reverence for the physical spaces associated with divine worship.
